headline: Regulated credit or a certificate? What your qualification is actually worth
description: Why two courses teaching the same technique can leave you holding different things, what the price gap is made of, when the cheaper course is the right buy, and four questions that tell you which you are being sold.

acceptedAnswer.text: A regulated course names it — VTCT, for every unit on our calendar. “Accredited” on its own is not an answer; it means a provider has been approved by somebody, not that your credit is recorded on a national framework.

Every regulated unit has one — UHB205, UNHB374 — and it identifies the exact standard you are assessed against. An attendance course has a course name and no code, because there is no national standard behind it.

A regulated unit carries the awarding body’s figure for the teaching, practice and supervised assessment it requires; ours run from {{cpd:minGlh}} to {{cpd:maxGlh}}. If the answer is “two days” rather than a number of guided hours, you are looking at contact time on an attendance course.

mainEntity.name: Does the credit count toward a full qualification, and which one?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regulated credit is recorded against you and banks toward a Diploma — it follows you if you move salons or come back to finish in five years. A certificate proves attendance and competence to the provider’s satisfaction and counts toward nothing else. Either can be the right buy, as long as it is the one you meant to buy.
